title: RBI Compounds Jusda India's Rs 18.5 Crore Share Issuance to a Land-Border Country Entity Without Government Approval
case_name: In re Jusda India Supply Chain Management Private Limited (FEMA compounding)
citation: Compounding order dated 8 April 2026, under Section 15, FEMA 1999
card_summary: Jusda India Supply Chain, part of the Foxconn group's logistics arm, issued shares worth about Rs 18.5 crore to entities linked to a land-border country, without the government approval such issuance needs. The ED filed a complaint under Section 6 of FEMA, then gave a no-objection for compounding after Jusda applied to the RBI under Section 15. The RBI compounded it on 8 April 2026, with a payment of Rs 12,52,984.
card_tip: Any share issuance or allotment to an investor from a country sharing a land border with India needs prior government approval under the FEMA Non-Debt Instruments Rules before the shares are issued, not after the fact.
verification_notes: The Rs 18.5 crore share issuance, the land-border country entities, the ED's Section 6 complaint and no-objection, the RBI's 8 April 2026 compounding order under Section 15 FEMA and the Rs 12,52,984 payment are corroborated across The420.in, Telangana Today and The Hans India reports of the same RBI order.
